import re
back = r"(a+)b\1"                       # some a's, a b, then the SAME a's again
for s in ["aba", "aabaa", "aaabaaa", "aabaaa", "abaa"]:
    print(f"  {s!r:10} {bool(re.fullmatch(back, s))}")
description: This pattern uses a backreference to require equal runs of a characters on both sides of b.

steps.description: back captures one or more a characters before b. The backreference \1 requires the same captured text after b.
The test strings include equal a runs and unequal a runs around b.

steps.answer: It will not match because the captured aa must reappear unchanged after b, but the string has aaa.
steps.question: Will 'aabaaa' match this pattern?

steps.description: fullmatch tests the entire string and bool converts the match result to True or False.
The loop prints the match result for the current test string.
